A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GEM research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original pre-training comparisons across nine downstream benchmarks, taxonomy predictability measurements, clustering ablations, and proxy-training experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds taxonomy-coherence measurements, GIS selection ablations, contamination testing, and parameter-sensitivity analyses.

M1.justification: The vMF mixture, uniform generative prior, balance objective, MM updates, GIS formula, and FastText distillation procedure remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 moves from Appendix I to J; newly disclosed defaults do not establish a method revision.

E1.justification: Appendix I.1 adds an evaluation scenario mixing natural web data with synthetic Cosmopedia content. The CommonCrawl pre-training coverage and nine downstream benchmarks remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Spherical K-Means, previously present in the clustering ablation, joins all three main Table 1 comparisons. New Table 4 compares GIS with random, confidence-only, and center-only selection. WebOrganizer Domain becoming Topic in the prose corrects its description rather than establishing a replacement comparator.

E3.justification: Supplementary evaluation protocols expand substantially: top-15 TF-IDF words with NPMI/CV metrics, five representatives per cluster followed by labeling 720 held-out samples, synthetic-contamination testing, and controlled sweeps over regularization and seed-corpus size. The original 1.1B-parameter, 25B-token training and downstream evaluation protocol remains unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained cluster-count, clustering-mechanism, and token-budget analyses, v2 adds quantitative coherence evaluation, GIS selection ablations, qualitative clustering cases, synthetic-contamination robustness, regularizer and seed-size sensitivity, and learned-concentration analysis in Appendices B.3–B.4 and I.

E5.justification: Both versions report ten train/test splits for the predictability analysis and the same median/IQR visualization. v2 adds no experimental repeat counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Table 10's concentration statistics describe variation across clusters, not uncertainty across experimental runs.

E6.justification: Existing downstream scores are retained, while Table 1 adds Spherical K-Means averages of 42.77, 42.78, and 40.63 under DoReMi, Perf, and RegMix. New findings include GIS labeling accuracy of 84.17% versus 80.41–81.67% for alternatives, coherence scores, sensitivity results, concentration summaries, and synthetic-contamination outcomes. These substantially expand the evidence without establishing performance gains between versions for retained GEM runs.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, objective, concentration lemma, regularizer proposition, MM derivation, and Appendix A convergence theorem and proof are unchanged. The added embedder-to-LLM geometry discussion is an informal applicability qualification.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about geometric partitioning, balance regularization, monotonic MM inference, scalable distillation, interpretability, and downstream improvements. Additional supporting experiments do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Section 3.1 now explicitly treats embedding geometry as a useful proxy rather than an exact equivalent of downstream LLM geometry. The discussion qualifies the 1.1B/25B setting as early-stage scaling evidence and recommends monitoring synthetic-content shifts. New appendix interpretations address prototype quality, parameter robustness, and directional compactness.

D1.justification: v2 newly discloses the default balance coefficient of 5000, its rationale relative to concentrations around 900, and the 3B-token seed default. Appendix E specifies Spherical K-Means normalization and centroid updates. Existing hardware, optimizer, training budgets, and distillation splits are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Cosmopedia and Binoculars citations supporting the contamination analysis and corrects WebOrganizer's description to LLM-derived topic labels. The related-work section and overall research positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Changes include targeted explanatory paragraphs, taxonomy spelling corrections, updated cross-references, and a conference publication footer. New appendix subsections and Appendix I extend the document, but the existing narrative and main section organization are largely retained.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands tabular presentation with new coherence, prototype-selection, regularization, seed-size, and concentration tables, and adds comparator rows throughout Table 1. Existing figures and detailed benchmark tables are retained with relocation or renumbering; Table 1 also corrects ranking emphasis.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's largely qualitative GIS validation, v2 provides direct coherence and representative-selection evidence, useful sensitivity controls, clearer defaults, and more explicit applicability limits. These strengthen empirical support and reproducibility. The gain is limited by underspecified contamination testing, including missing mixture proportions and quantitative GEM balance measurements, and absent uncertainty estimates for the new accuracy comparisons.
